items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It is a non-governmental organisation.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
items.answer: UNESCO – education, science and culture
items.markingKey: (a) UNESCO – education, science and culture. UNHCR – refugees; FAO – food and agriculture; ILO – labour standards are the correct pairs for the others.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about UN reform and India's case for a Security Council seat:
I. All member countries agree on India's permanent membership.
II. Suggested criteria for new members include being a major economic or military power, contributions to the UN budget and peacekeeping, being a large nation and respecting democracy and human rights.
III. India has never participated in UN peacekeeping.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (a) I is incorrect: Some countries, including Pakistan, oppose it. II is correct. III is incorrect: India is one of the largest contributors of troops to UN peacekeeping.

items.stem: What is meant by 'UN Charter' in the context of international organisations and the evolution of the UN?
items.answer: The founding document of the United Nations, signed by 50 countries at San Francisco in June 1945.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: UN Charter correctly explained as the founding document of the United Nations, signed by 50 countries at San Francisco in June 1945.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about principal organs and agencies of the UN:
I. The Secretary-General is the representative of the UN as a whole.
II. The Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994 after the last trust territory became independent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on international organisations and the evolution of the UN and answer the questions that follow.
"The UN was set up to prevent international conflict and to facilitate cooperation among states. International organisations help with matters of war and peace and help countries cooperate to make better lives. 24 October is celebrated as United Nations Day."
(i) The predecessor of the United Nations was the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'international organisation' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The UN is regarded as the most important international organisation. (2)
items.answer: (i) League of Nations (ii) A body created by states to cooperate on issues such as war and peace, development and the environment. (iii) Almost all independent states are members and it deals with a wide range of issues from peace to development.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) League of Nations (ii) A body created by states to cooperate on issues such as war and peace, development and the environment. (iii) Almost all independent states are members and it deals with a wide range of issues from peace to development.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about other international organisations:
I. The IAEA's inspectors regularly visit nuclear facilities to ensure that civilian reactors are not used for military purposes.
II. Amnesty International is a specialised agency of the UN.
III. The WTO's decisions are taken unanimously, but major economic powers dominate its rule-making.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is incorrect: It is a non-governmental organisation. III is correct.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about other international organisations:
I. Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch are non-governmental organisations.
II. The WTO's decisions are taken unanimously, but major economic powers dominate its rule-making.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about principal organs and agencies of the UN:
I. The five permanent members of the Security Council are the USA, Russia, the UK, France and China.
II. All members of the Security Council have veto power.
III. The non-permanent members do not have the veto power.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is incorrect: Only the five permanent members have veto power. III is correct.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"India supports the strengthening and revitalisation of the UN in the changed world. Reform of the UN involves reforming the organisation's structures and processes and reviewing the issues it handles. Suggested criteria for new members include being a major economic or military power, contributions to the UN budget and peacekeeping, being a large nation and respecting democracy and human rights. India's claim is opposed by some countries, including Pakistan, due to rivalry."
(i) Explain the term 'UN reform', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Expanding the Security Council is difficult. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Security Council has been expanded several times since 1992 to add permanent members." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) Changes proposed in the structure and processes of the UN, especially the expansion of the Security Council. (ii) Members disagree on criteria and the permanent members are reluctant to share their privileges. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: No new permanent members have been added since 1945.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Changes proposed in the structure and processes of the UN, especially the expansion of the Security Council. (ii) Members disagree on criteria and the permanent members are reluctant to share their privileges. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: No new permanent members have been added since 1945.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about international organisations and the evolution of the UN:
I. The UN was founded as a successor to the League of Nations after the Second World War.
II. 24 October is celebrated as United Nations Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The WTO is criticised by developing countries.
Reason (R): Major economic powers such as the US and EU use it to frame trade rules in their interest.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: major economic powers such as the US and EU use it to frame trade rules in their interest.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of these was a criterion suggested for new permanent members of the Security Council?
items.answer: Contribution to the UN budget
items.markingKey: (c) Contribution to the UN budget.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on principal organs and agencies of the UN and answer the questions that follow.
"The General Assembly includes all member states, each with one vote. The non-permanent members do not have the veto power. The five permanent members of the Security Council are the USA, Russia, the UK, France and China."
(i) Non-permanent members of the UN Security Council are elected for a term of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'veto' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The veto power is criticised. (2)
items.answer: (i) two years (ii) The power of a permanent member of the Security Council to block a decision by voting against it. (iii) It allows any one of the five permanent members to block decisions, even if the others agree.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) two years (ii) The power of a permanent member of the Security Council to block a decision by voting against it. (iii) It allows any one of the five permanent members to block decisions, even if the others agree.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about principal organs and agencies of the UN is correct?
items.answer: The Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994 after the last trust territory became independent.
items.markingKey: (a) The others are wrong: Only the five permanent members have veto power. They are elected for two-year terms. It is located at The Hague.
options: The Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994 after the last trust territory became independent.
Non-permanent members of the Security Council are elected for five years.
The International Court of Justice is located in New York.
All members of the Security Council have veto power.

items.stem: The following statement about international organisations and the evolution of the UN is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The UN Charter was signed at Geneva."
items.answer: It was signed at San Francisco in June 1945.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It was signed at San Francisco in June 1945.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.
